newsitem.title: USA: US Q3 rail car fleet highest in 8 years--AAR.
newsitem.headline: US Q3 rail car fleet highest in 8 years--AAR.

text.p: The nation's rail car fleet grew to 1,232,674 in the third quarter of this year to its highest level since 1988, the Association of American Railroads said Thursday.
The fleet size was up 0.5 percent from the second quarter and grew 1.5 percent from the third quarter of 1995.

The AAR said railroads, shippers and private car companies added 14,881 new cars in the third quarter, up 6.0 percent from the third quarter of 1995. In the first nine months of 1996, 43,700 new cars were added to the fleet, down 5.8 percent from the same period last year.

A total of 822 rebuilt cars were installed in the third quarter, down from 1,866 a year earlier. In the first nine months of the year, 1,857 rebuilt cars were added, down from 4,286 in the same period of 1995, the AAR said.
The total number of freight cars on order and undelivered stood at 24,000 as of Oct 1, down from 34,834 a year ago.
Railroads added 97 new locomotives and 35 rebuilt units to their fleets in the third quarter, down from 156 new locomotives and 39 rebuilt units a year earlier, AAR said.
For the nine months, new locomotive additions fell to 504 from 705 in the same period last year, and rebuilt deliveries fell to 92 from 112.
